# TODO — Minor Task List (Active Tasks)

**Tier 2 of 3** — the MINOR task list. Holds active tasks (pending + in_progress) at the day-to-day work grain. Each minor task lives under a major milestone in `docs/ROADMAP.md` and decomposes further into entries in `docs/DECOMPOSED.md` when YOLO mode picks it up.

Completed tasks move to `docs/FINALIZED.md` per `.claude/CONSTRAINTS.md §FINALIZED BEFORE DELETE`. Never delete a task description; only flip status (LAW: NEVER DELETE TODO INFO).

Status markers:
- `[ ]` pending
- `[~]` in_progress
- `[x]` complete (move to FINALIZED.md immediately, never leave here)

LAW #0 reminder: every task description preserves the user's verbatim words.

**Three-tier cascade:** ROADMAP.md (major) → TODO.md (minor, this file) → DECOMPOSED.md (decomposed). YOLO mode reads all three and works the cascade — see `.claude/skills/yolo/SKILL.md` and `.claude/WORKFLOW.md §YOLO MODE`.

**Verbatim user ask:** > "ultrathink is there anything missing anything not automatic setup flow anything not working anything forgotten. is the setup going to produce the running bot doe the setup auto find the server ip and set it up or does the user enter it .. all these type of questions need to be resolved in the todo writeup of finalization work"

Super-review pass surfaced 20 findings against the 4-milestone consolidated work. Categorized by severity. Each must close before V4 is "production-ready" per the user's stated intent.

### Critical / High — must ship before any production deploy

- [x] **HIGH — Revert `message_handler.py` regression + delete dead config helpers.** — Closed 2026-05-19. Reverted to inline `'code' in user_message or 'script' in user_message`. Deleted `code_keywords`, `image_keywords`, `is_code_request`, `is_image_request`, `extract_image_prompt`, `memory_regex`, `url_regex`, `code_block_regex` from `config.py`. Wiring `self.config.is_code_request()` introduced false positives on conversational words ("class", "function", "method", "program"). Original inline `'code' in user_message or 'script' in user_message` was conservative; the `code_keywords` list was speculative dead code. Revert to inline check. DELETE `code_keywords`, `image_keywords`, `is_code_request`, `is_image_request`, `extract_image_prompt`, `memory_regex`, `url_regex` from `config.py`. Cleanup milestone closes by deleting dead code, not wiring it. Fixes regression introduced 2026-05-19.

- [x] **HIGH — Patch Pollinations auth (belt-and-suspenders).** — Closed 2026-05-19. `config.py` new-stack now sets `self.api_url = f"{GEN_CHAT_URL}?key={raw_key}"` and same for `models_url` + `image_models_url`. Bearer header stays primary, `?key=` is the safety-net fallback per PolliLibPy v2.1.5 pattern. `config.py` new-stack `api_url = GEN_CHAT_URL` carries no API key — relies purely on `Authorization: Bearer` header. PolliLibPy (the reference) uses BOTH header AND `?key=<key>` query string. If Pollinations enforces `?key=` in any edge case, V4 fails 401. Action: append `?key=<raw_key>` to `chat_url`, `models_url`, `image_models_url` in new-stack branch. Bearer header stays primary, `?key=` is fallback.

- [x] **HIGH — Setup does NOT validate keys live (user intent — "is setup going to produce the running bot").** — Closed 2026-05-19. `configure.py` got `validate_keys_live()` — hits Discord `/users/@me` (token) + `/applications/@me` (intents flags) + Pollinations `/text/models` (key + model count). Runs automatically at end of interactive flow. Available standalone via `python configure.py --validate`. Prints ✓/✗ per check + actionable error messages. `configure.py` writes `.env` but never verifies Discord token via `GET https://discord.com/api/v10/users/@me` or Pollinations key via `GET https://gen.pollinations.ai/text/models`. User finds out keys are bad only when starting the bot. Action: add `validate_keys_live()` automatically at end of interactive flow — hit both APIs, print bot username + model count on success, fail-loud with fix hints on failure.

- [x] **HIGH — Setup does NOT auto-find server IP (user intent — "does the setup auto find the server ip").** — Closed 2026-05-19. `configure.py` got `detect_network()` — public IPv4 via api.ipify.org with 2 fallback endpoints (api64.ipify.org, icanhazip.com), local IPv4 via UDP-socket trick (avoids 127.0.1.1 from /etc/hosts). Runs automatically. Available standalone via `python configure.py --detect-network`. Smoke-tested live: public `199.87.141.189`, local `192.168.1.62`. configure.py prompts for nothing IP-related. CLOUDFLARE.md tells user to manually `curl ifconfig.me`. Action: add `detect_network()` to configure.py — `requests.get("https://api.ipify.org").text` for public IPv4 + `socket.gethostbyname(socket.gethostname())` for local. Display both in final step + save as informational `.env` comments (`DETECTED_PUBLIC_IP`, `DETECTED_LOCAL_IP`).

- [x] **HIGH — Setup does NOT start the bot (user intent — "automatic setup flow").** — Closed 2026-05-19 (configure.py side; web UI bot-lifecycle endpoints deferred to a follow-up). `configure.py` got `start_bot_subprocess()` — launches `python bot.py` in subprocess, tails stdout for 15s looking for "connected to Discord" line, writes PID to `logs/bot.pid` on success. Prompted automatically at end of interactive flow IF Discord + Pollinations both validated OK. Available standalone via `python configure.py --start-bot`. configure.py exits after writing `.env`. Web wizard transitions to chat (Pollinations only — Discord bot NOT running). User has no way to tell if "setup complete" = "Discord bot online" or "web chat works against Pollinations only." Action: configure.py final step prompts "Start the bot now and tail logs for 10s? [Y/n]" — on Y, `subprocess.Popen([python, "bot.py"])`, stream output, check for "connected to Discord!" log line, report status. Web wizard: add "Discord Bot Status" panel + ▶ Start Bot button via `POST /api/bot/start` backend endpoint.

- [x] **HIGH — No Discord OAuth2 invite URL generated.** — Closed 2026-05-19. After token validation via `/users/@me`, `validate_keys_live()` extracts the bot's `id` and builds invite URL `https://discord.com/oauth2/authorize?client_id={bot_id}&permissions=534723950656&scope=bot%20applications.commands`. Permissions bitfield 534723950656 = Send Messages + Send Messages in Threads + Read Message History + Attach Files + Add Reactions + Embed Links + Use External Emojis + Use Slash Commands + View Channels. Displayed prominently in validation output + final "Next steps" section as step 0. Even after token is created, user must manually compute the invite URL in Discord developer portal. Trivially automatable from the `/users/@me` response (gives bot's user ID). Action: after token validation, build invite URL `https://discord.com/oauth2/authorize?client_id={bot_id}&permissions=534723950656&scope=bot` (Send Messages + Read Message History + Attach Files + Add Reactions + Embed Links + Use Slash Commands) and display prominently as a clickable link (terminal) / button (web wizard).

- [x] **HIGH — Cloudflare integration is 100% manual (user intent — "automatic setup flow"/"whatever we have to do needs to be explained").** — Closed 2026-05-19. `configure.py --setup-cloudflare-tunnel` shipped — 7-step automated flow: (1) detects cloudflared, offers apt/brew/winget install if missing; (2) `cloudflared tunnel login` (only manual step — opens browser); (3) `tunnel create unity-bot-prod`, captures UUID via `--output json` with fallback to `tunnel list` if name already exists; (4) prompts hostname (default `www.unity.unityailab.com`), runs `tunnel route dns` (creates CNAME automatically) with manual-fallback instructions on failure; (5) writes `/etc/cloudflared/config.yml` (Linux/macOS, via sudo if needed) or `~/.cloudflared/config.yml` (Windows) from template substituting tunnel UUID + hostname + WEB_UI_PORT; copies credentials into /etc/cloudflared on Linux + chmods 600; (6) runs `service install` + starts via systemd / Windows SCM / launchd; (7) prints verification curl command. CLOUDFLARE.md §1.0 added pointing at the automation as the primary path; §1.1-§1.6 remain as the recovery / customization fallback. Cross-platform. CLOUDFLARE.md is comprehensive doc but no automation. Action: add `configure.py --setup-cloudflare-tunnel` (or web wizard "Connect to Cloudflare" button) that detects `cloudflared` on PATH (offers `apt install` / `winget install` if missing), runs `cloudflared tunnel login` (browser-based — user's ONLY manual step), runs `tunnel create unity-bot-prod`, captures UUID via `--output json`, prompts hostname (default `www.unity.unityailab.com`), runs `route dns`, writes `/etc/cloudflared/config.yml` from template, runs `service install`, verifies via `curl -I https://<hostname>/api/health`.

- [x] **MEDIUM — Combined-mode config split-brain.** — Closed 2026-05-19. `bot.py` got `_reload_config_on_sighup()` handler — re-loads dotenv, builds new Config + APIClient, wires into message_handler + memory_manager, closes old APIClient on bot.loop. Registered via `signal.signal(SIGHUP, ...)` (POSIX-only — Windows still needs full restart). `bot.py:on_ready` writes PID to `logs/bot.pid`. `web_server.py:_signal_bot_reload()` reads the PID + sends SIGHUP after `/api/setup` save. - [x] **MEDIUM — `_load_config()` race + APIClient leak.** — Closed 2026-05-19. Added module-level `_config_lock = threading.Lock()` and wrapped the entire `_load_config()` body in `with _config_lock:`. Now serializes concurrent reloads. Before reassigning `_api_client`, captures the old reference and calls `run_async(old_client.close())` to drain its aiohttp ClientSession — eliminates the file-descriptor leak on every reload. Concurrent requests can both trigger `_load_config()` simultaneously — both create new Config + APIClient instances, old aiohttp.ClientSession dropped without `.close()`. Resource leak under load. Action: wrap `_load_config` body in `threading.Lock()`. Before reassigning `_api_client`, call `run_async(_api_client.close())` on the old instance.
